newsitem.title: GREECE: BOMB ROCKS CENTRAL ATHENS ENGINEERING SCHOOL.
newsitem.headline: BOMB ROCKS CENTRAL ATHENS ENGINEERING SCHOOL.

text.p: A bomb blast rocked the central Athens engineering school on Wednesday but there were no reports of injuries due to a telephoned warning, police said.
The blast was caused by a timebomb on the second floor of the Athens Polytechnic School, police said.

The Polytechnic is the scene of clashes between police and hooligans around November 17 every year as Greece prepares to commemorate a student uprising which helped bring down a 1967-74 military junta.
The junta sent tanks into the Polytechnic on November 17, 1973, and ruthlessly crushed the uprising, killing a number of students.
Police said the caller who warned that the bomb was about to go off did not claim responsibility on behalf of any particular organisation. --Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
